items.prompt: An L-shaped garden is made by cutting a 5 m by 3 m rectangle out of one corner of a 12 m by 8 m rectangle. What is the area of the garden in square metres?
hints: Find the area of the big rectangle first.
Take away the corner that was cut out.
items.explanation: The big rectangle is 12 × 8 = 96. The corner is 5 × 3 = 15. The garden is 96 − 15 = 81 square metres.

items.prompt: A garden is a 12 m by 8 m rectangle with a 5 m by 3 m rectangle cut from one corner. What is the perimeter of the garden in metres?
hints: Draw the shape and mark all its sides.
Cutting a corner adds new edges, but it also removes edges.
The new edges are as long as the edges they replace.
items.explanation: Cutting out a corner keeps the perimeter the same, because the two new edges are as long as the two edges they replace. So the perimeter is 2 × (12 + 8) = 40 m.

items.prompt: A rectangle has a perimeter of 54 cm and a length of 16 cm. What is its area in square centimetres?
hints: Half the perimeter is length plus width.
Multiply the length by the width.
items.explanation: Length plus width is 27 cm, so the width is 27 − 16 = 11 cm. The area is 16 × 11 = 176 cm².

items.prompt: True or false: A shape made from a 6 cm by 4 cm rectangle joined to a 3 cm by 2 cm rectangle has an area of 30 cm².
hints: Find the area of each rectangle.

items.prompt: True or false: A rectangle with an area of 36 cm² and a width of 4 cm has a length of 8 cm.
hints: Divide the area by the width.
items.explanation: 36 ÷ 4 = 9, so the length is 9 cm. 4 × 8 would only be 32.
